title: Curbing Cyber Fraud - The Rising Nepal
description: Curbing Cyber Fraud  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
With the rapid development in information technology, digital transactions have become easier. People use digital wallets in everyday life, making it convenient for everyday financial operations. However, it has exposed citizens to increasingly sophisticated forms of cyber fraud. People should be very careful when trading digitally, including using mobile banking, digital wallets and online payments. Equally responsible should be the state. The rising cyber fraud should be taken as a serious concern legally and must be stopped at any cost.





Financial loss caused by cyber fraud in Nepal is rising alarmingly. According to the Nepal Police Cyber Bureau, people lost more than Rs. 2 billion to cyber fraud during the last fiscal year, while only around Rs. 180 million was recovered. The recovery rate over the past three years has reportedly remained at approximately eight per cent. These figures suggest that the country needs a sturdy response strategy to fight such crimes. Only arresting culprits is not enough. The stolen money should also be recovered to give justice to the victims.





The proposed Integrated Cyber Scam Response Centre is a positive initiative from the state. Proper coordination between the police, banks, financial institutions, telecommunications companies and payment service providers under a common mechanism strengthens the existing system. Criminals mostly involve several institutions to transfer stolen money making it difficult for authorities to track on time.





Police officials have pointed out that the first hour after a fraudulent transaction is very crucial for recovering the money. It becomes difficult to investigate if the victims report incidents outside banking hours or during public holidays. A system that depends on conventional office hours cannot respond to crimes that can take place at any time. Digital service providers must establish a twenty-four-hour mechanism to receive requests from law enforcement agencies. They should also be able to freeze suspicious transactions.





The introduction of a specialised centre alone will not resolve the problem. It requires proper execution, adequate legal authority, capable human resources and dynamic coordination between institutions. Difficult legal procedures must be made easy to establish standardised protocols for sharing information and responding to fraud complaints. Banking and digital wallet institutions should also be held accountable for delays in responding to legitimate requests from the authorities. There should be thorough investigations to catch the criminals while safeguarding innocent account holders.





Along with manpower, adequate investigative technology is essential. Cyber fraud nowadays has evolved technically, involving multiple accounts and digital platforms that can be operated from any corner of the world. Nepal Police needs trained investigators, digital forensic experts and modern technological tools to trace transactions and identify perpetrators. The proposed operation should be supported by sufficient personnel and resources. The most challenging aspect of cyber fraud is its cross-border nature. Digital money can quickly move through Nepal’s financial system, making recovery difficult. Cross-country cooperation for faster mechanisms for tracing funds, sharing intelligence and investigations must be implemented. The experiences of countries including India, China, Thailand and Singapore, studied by the Nepal Police, should be adapted to Nepal’s institutional context.





Only catching crime is not the solution. There must be proper public awareness campaigns for theft prevention. Criminals use techniques including phishing, fraudulent investment schemes, impersonation and sending hacked online links. Digital payment service providers should strengthen transaction monitoring and alert systems. Customers should also be able to report suspicious activities easily. Digital service providers can thrive by providing digital literacy and financial security to their users. Public confidence in digital financial services will improve if they are assured that citizens will receive timely assistance when fraud occurs. The government must ensure that the proposed centre becomes an effective mechanism for responding immediately to complaints. The success must be measured by faster action, stronger accountability and assured relief for victims.

title: Former Nepal PM charged in land swap case — Kathmandu Post - UA.NEWS
description: Former Nepal PM charged in land swap case — Kathmandu Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
In Nepal, the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has filed an indictment with the Special Court against former Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal, former minister and Nepali Congress leader Minendra Rijal, and another 95 people. The case was opened over a reportedly illegal swap and sale of state land in Morang district, Kathmandu Post reports.

The CIAA is seeking compensation for damages amounting to 734.956 million Nepalese rupees, prison sentences and fines, as well as the confiscation of land plots transferred under the disputed scheme. According to the commission, these plots should have been confiscated and kept in state or public ownership.

Terms of land use

At the center of the case is Rijal Canning and Company. It was allowed to retain about 40 hectares of land in Morang above the legally established landholding limit, on the condition that it operated a fruit-processing enterprise. The CIAA claims that the company did not use the land for that purpose, and therefore the government decided to confiscate it in 1992.

However, according to the commission, the company was later allowed to exchange two plots in Biratnagar with a total area of about 2.9 hectares for land of equal area in Banigama, Morang district. According to the indictment, the company bought the land in Banigama for 1.285 million rupees and sold the two plots in Biratnagar for 83.8625 million rupees. The difference between the recorded prices was 82.5775 million rupees.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Government committee decision

The CIAA investigation found that restrictions on the two plots were lifted on August 28, 2006, after then land reform official Umanath Pandey interpreted a Supreme Court ruling. The commission believes this paved the way for the subsequent exchange, although the land was not used for the declared industrial activity.

The exchange process intensified in 2009. In November, the Ministry of Land Reform and Management submitted a proposal to the Cabinet, which referred it to the Social Committee. According to the indictment, the committee approved the exchange on December 1. The CIAA accuses Rijal, who coordinated the committee at the time, of approving the proposal despite the company’s alleged violation of the conditions for exemption from the landholding limit.

Of the 97 defendants, the CIAA classified 46 people, including Nepal and Rijal, as those considered directly involved in the alleged offense. Others were included in the case to recover the claimed damages or confiscate property. This is the second corruption case against Nepal: in June 2025, the CIAA charged him and another 92 people in a case involving land belonging to Patanjali Yogpeeth and Ayurveda Company Nepal. Nepal denied wrongdoing.

title: Nepal, West Asia Share Atmospheric Link - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal, West Asia Share Atmospheric Link  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Nepal and West Asia share atmospheric connections that matter for mountain climate. Published research identifies sources of Middle Eastern soot that reach the Himalayas and Tibet, contributing to decreased albedo through the deposition of impurities. Read together, these findings establish connectivity between the two regions, but more research is needed to quantify West Asia’s sole contribution to the warming of Nepal’s Himalayas. This connection provides an evidence-based starting point for dialogue and climate diplomacy.

Nepal’s temperature record establishes the problem independently of the contributions from its distant sources. A group of scientists analysed 30 stations in Nepal for 1976–2015 and reported average increases of approximately 0.45° C per decade in daily maximum temperature and 0.09° C in daily minimum temperature. However, these are historical temperature trends from a station network, not measurements of present warming at Himalayan summits or estimates of the Gulf's contribution to Himalayan warming.

Atmospheric chemistry

Atmospheric chemistry operates through various processes. For greenhouse gases, the IPCC establishes a near-linear relationship between cumulative human carbon dioxide emissions and the global warming they cause. This global relationship does not provide a Nepal-specific allocation of warming among emitting countries. Greenhouse gas-induced warming and the effect of transported particles on snow require different forms of attribution.

For soot, atmospheric models link specific emission regions to receiving locations. It has been observed that northern India and central China supplied most of the black carbon to Himalayan locations across different seasons. Studies have traced black carbon particles in the Nepali and Tibetan Himalayas that have the origin in the Gulf region. Black carbon is the light-absorbing component of soot, and its deposition on snow can reduce the snow’s reflectivity and, as a result, accelerate melting.

A later modeling study by a group of Chinese and Western scientists placed South Asian biomass, biofuel, and fossil-fuel emissions at the center of Himalayan black-carbon pollution. Contributions from Central Asian and Middle Eastern fossil-fuel sources were relatively more important in the northwestern Tibetan Plateau, particularly in summer. Nevertheless, the findings for that plateau cannot be directly applied to a particular glacier in Nepal. Specific geographic locations and the geographic part of the findings are yet to be established.

Nepal provides direct evidence of impurities in snow. Samples collected on Mera La Glacier in Solukhumbu in 2009 found that 6–10 per cent of the black carbon originated from the Gulf region. Due to the reduction in albedo, the estimated additional energy absorption was 75–120 watts per square meter. These figures show that a snow-covered surface absorbs solar radiation, but it is difficult to quantify the West Asian contribution specifically.

Dust adds another layer of contributors to warming and snow melting. Seasonal atmospheric transport of dust from the Arabian Peninsula towards the Indian subcontinent, including elevated transport over the Arabian Sea, has been reported several times. This establishes a transport pathway to the Himalayas. However, identifying Arab-origin material at a particular Nepali glacier requires evidence at the receiving location. Combining a transport study with a snow-darkening study does not, by itself, determine the deposited material’s origin unless more detailed material studies are done.

Atmospheric circulation also carries moisture. Various studies describe western condensation nuclei traveling eastward along the subtropical westerly jet and bringing precipitation primarily to the western Himalaya, Karakoram, and Hindu Kush. Multiple lines of evidence identify the Arabian Sea as their principal moisture source, with contributions from the Mediterranean and Eurasian lakes. Together, these studies distinguish three related measures: emissions at the source, atmospheric transport, and effects on the snow surface. Inventories estimate emissions, transport models project where material travels, and snow sampling with radiative modelling assesses local effects. Attributing impacts to Nepal requires linking all three measures for the same location and period. Future site-specific studies of Middle Eastern contributions across the Himalayas could provide actionable evidence.

There is also documented scope for emissions mitigation. Various analyses of 2019 satellite imagery and modelling establish human-caused methane emissions across the Middle East, North Africa, and the Himalayas. Their estimate exceeded prior inventories by 35 per cent; oil and gas accounted for 38 per cent of the total. Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar met the study’s 0.2 per cent upstream methane-intensity benchmark, demonstrating performance variation within the region.

Scientific value

For Nepal, the diplomatic implication is a case for cooperation grounded in identifiable emissions and testable atmospheric connections. The evidence supports the inclusion of West Asian partners while maintaining a focus on major South Asian soot sources. Connecting source inventories, seasonal transport, and measurements of Nepali snow offers a research agenda to quantify contributions that remain unresolved in the cited studies. Its scientific value lies in making the attribution measurable, with location, season, and uncertainty explicit.

Guided by non-alignment and Panchsheel’s five principles of peaceful coexistence, Nepal can advance climate diplomacy inspired by the aspiration of a Zone of Peace proposal, which was initiated in Nepal in 1975. These values offer a constructive basis for engaging West Asian and South Asian partners in joint atmospheric research, cleaner energy, climate mitigation, and mountain adaptation. Cooperation should acknowledge scientific and knowledge gaps while pursuing measurable reductions in harmful emissions. Protecting Himalayan glaciers, water security, and livelihoods can thus become a shared investment in regional stability, mutual benefit, and lasting global peace.





(Dr. Bhattarai is a Professor of Geography at the University of Central Missouri, Warrensburg, MO, USA. Dr. Adhikari is an Honorary Distinguished Fellow at the Institute for Integrated Development Studies (IIDS), Nepal.)

According to him, he is not only trying to hit sixes, but also watches the bowlers' actions and assesses the situation after the first balls.

Goals in the T20 format

After arriving at the NPL, Russell surpassed the mark of 10,000 runs in T20 matches. He said that five years ago he set himself the goal of becoming the first fast-bowling all-rounder to reach 10,000 runs and 500 wickets in T20. The cricketer named 12,000 runs in this format as his new personal goal.

description: NTB to hold Kukur Tihar reel contest  The Rising Nepal

full_article:
By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Nov. 4: The Nepal Tourism Board (NTB) is set to organise the first-ever Kukur Tihar Reel Competition 2026 to promote Nepal’s traditional festivals and cultural heritage through digital platforms.

According to the press release issued by NTB on Tuesday, the competition is part of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Khadak Raj Paudel’s initiative to promote Nepal’s tourism internationally by highlighting its unique cultural traditions.

The initiative follows the installation of traditional bamboo swings (linge ping) at 100 locations across the country during Dashain, in collaboration with local governments and tourism-related organisations.

The competition aims to showcase the cultural significance of Kukur Tihar, the close bond between humans and dogs, and Nepal’s traditions to international audiences through creative digital content.

Interested participants are required to create original and creative reels related to Kukur Tihar and publish them on their Instagram or Facebook accounts. The creator of the best reel will receive a cash prize of Rs. 100,000.

Kukur Tihar, celebrated on the second day of Tihar, is a traditional festival in which dogs are worshipped with tika, flower garlands and special food. Dogs are honoured in Nepali culture as symbols of loyalty, security and companionship.

According to the competition guidelines, all video reels must be in English or include English subtitles or an English voice-over. Participants must use the prescribed hashtags, tag the relevant tourism-related accounts and submit their videos through a Google Drive link with downloading and viewing access.

The videos must be original creations. The Tourism Board may also use the submitted content for tourism promotion and digital communication through its various platforms.

The deadline for submission is November 21, 2026.

The competition seeks to present Kukur Tihar not only as a religious and cultural celebration but also as a reflection of Nepal's love and respect for animals and the spirit of coexistence. It is expected to encourage young content creators and help promote Nepal's cultural tourism to a wider international audience.

title: How CPC Perseveres Rugorous Self-governance? - The Rising Nepal
description: How CPC Perseveres Rugorous Self-governance?  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) held its fifth plenary session in Beijing from October 26 to 29, 2026. This was an important meeting held at a critical juncture, marking the 105th anniversary of the founding of the CPC and a critical period in the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The Central Committee heard and discussed a report on the work of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presented by Comrade Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, on behalf of the Political Bureau. They also deliberated and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. All this demonstrates the CPC's firm confidence and strong resolve to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance through higher standards and more concrete measures.

To do a good job of governing the country, we must first do a good job of governing the Party, and that means governing it strictly. Full and rigorous Party self-governance is not about making efforts at isolated points. Rather, it requires taking strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle, ensuring that all aspects of Party building advance in a coordinated way and that all policies and measures are well-aligned and mutually reinforcing, and ensuring strict principles, measures, and atmosphere in every aspect and all stages of Party building.

Missions and tasks

Persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance means serving the Party's missions and tasks. At present, momentous changes of a magnitude not seen in a century are unfolding across the world at a faster pace. On the one hand, the historical trends of peace, development, cooperation, and mutual benefit are unstoppable; on the other hand, the deficits in peace, development, security, and governance are growing. Humanity faces unprecedented opportunities and challenges. The CPC is dedicated to pursuing happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. It is also dedicated to human progress and world harmony. Always guided by its missions and tasks, the CPC continues working to purify, improve, renew, and excel itself, breaking new ground in the self-reform of a century-old Party, and ensuring that the Party remains at the forefront of the times and maintains the historic initiative.

Persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance means adopting a problem-oriented approach. Problems are the voice of the times. Only by taking the resolution of prominent problems within the Party as the focus of our efforts and never shying away from problems can we strengthen Party building by correcting deviations, addressing irregularities, and promoting healthy practices. In the face of risks and tests under new historical conditions, the CPC has maintained a tough stance against corruption, strengthened checks on and oversight over the exercise of power, fortified the cultural-ethical foundations for upholding integrity and resisting corruption, and enhanced the overall efficacy of taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption. Since the 18th CPC National Congress, discipline inspection and supervision organs across the country have filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people, including 963 officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee. We have achieved an overwhelming victory and fully consolidated the gains in our fight against corruption.

Persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance means adhering to a top-down approach. Leading officials are the key few in advancing the cause of the Party and the country, and they serve as a weathervane for the whole Party and society. Since the 18th CPC National Congress, the CPC Central Committee, with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, has taken the formulation and implementation of the central Party leadership's eight-point decision on improving work conduct as the point of departure, starting with the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and applying strict standards first to high-ranking officials, so that leading officials, or the key few, set an example for those below them, generating powerful momentum for strictness to cascade down through the ranks. In the drafting of the Resolution, General Secretary Xi Jinping personally served as head of the drafting group, arranged for opinions to be extensively solicited from all sides, and successively chaired two symposiums to solicit opinions, three meetings of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, and two meetings of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, charting the course for full and rigorous Party self-governance.

Regulations

Persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance means running the Party according to regulations. Strengthening Party regulations and institutions represents a long-term, fundamental strategy for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance. As of the end of December 2025, the CPC had 3,372 intra-Party regulations in effect, about 80 per cent of which had been formulated or revised since the 18th CPC National Congress. The CPC has continued to improve the framework of Party regulations and institutions, ensure the enforcement of institutions, and eliminate hidden rules. It has educated Party members and officials and required them to correct their thinking and conduct in accordance with Party regulations and discipline. It has also encouraged officials to pursue reform and innovation and strive for success within the boundaries of regulations and discipline, and to foster and act on the correct view of performance. In this way, ideological Party building and regulation-based Party self-governance advance in tandem.

General Secretary Xi Jinping has pointed out, “Political parties are the leading and driving force for modernisation. Their values, ability to lead and govern, ethos, willpower and character have a direct bearing on the orientation and future of the modernization process.” China and Nepal are friendly neighbours connected by mountains and rivers with a time-honoured friendship, and inter-party exchanges between the two countries have been rich in content and fruitful in results. Under the new circumstances, both China and Nepal face the important task of accelerating national development and improving the lives of the people. China stands ready to work with Nepal to further strengthen exchanges of experience in Party building and state governance and administration, continuously improve governing capacity and governance performance, advance the China-Nepal strategic partnership of cooperation, and deliver greater benefits to the people of the two countries.





(The author is the Chinese Ambassador to Nepal.)

title: Flood risk persists after southwest storms - The Rising Nepal
description: Flood risk persists after southwest storms  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
New York, Nov. 4: The skies were clearing, but the risk of flooding remained over parts of the U.S. Southwest after powerful downpours sent massive amounts of water surging over the usually dry landscape, forcing hundreds to evacuate and keeping swift-water rescue teams busy.

Officials said cleanup and repair efforts could take weeks. One person died in the floodwaters and police suspect a second death was weather-related.

The National Weather Service said Monday that isolated cloudbursts were still possible across the Four Corners region — where New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado and Utah meet — as the phenomenon stoked by warming Pacific waters known as El Niño disrupts weather patterns.

Damage was widespread in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, a town of about 2,000. Officials feared the San Juan River that flows through it would top a level that nearly wiped out the town in 1911. The river reached 16.81 feet (5.1 meters) Sunday — a foot lower than the historic level — flooding downtown streets before receding Monday, the weather service said.

An entire home was lifted from its foundation and floated down the river before crashing into a pedestrian bridge. A section of a road bridge west of town crumbled under raging waters, said Archuleta County Sheriff's Office spokesperson Vicki Shaffer.

Dozens of people were rescued across the region, including some by helicopter. Shaffer said first responders were searching for people who may be stranded. "That will continue, just like last week, until we're sure that everybody who was trapped by the floodwaters has been rescued," she said.

The Colorado Department of Transportation reopened several closed bridges and roadways late Monday. Shaffer said evacuation orders remain in place, though she wasn't sure how many people were affected.

Pagosa Springs had just lifted an evacuation order from a previous storm, only to reimpose it Saturday. More than 20 trillion gallons of rain have fallen on the Four Corners states and Nevada in the past two weeks, according to calculations by former National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration chief scientist Ryan Maue.

With Election Day coming, officials in Colorado and Utah arranged alternative voting plans for evacuated or stranded residents. Utah said Monday that residents of hard-hit San Juan County will be allowed to vote electronically because some of them may not be able to reach polling places.

title: Two die of altitude sickness in Mustang - The Rising Nepal
description: Two die of altitude sickness in Mustang  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By Our Correspondent,Mustang, Nov. 4: Two Nepali nationals have died of suspected altitude sickness in Mustang within a period of two weeks, prompting local authorities to intensify awareness campaigns to prevent altitude-related illnesses among tourists.

The victims were a 67-year-old pilgrim, Tikaram Sharma, of Bareng Rural Municipality-2, Baglung, and a 27-year-old trekking guide, Lakchandra Kulung, of Mahakulung Rural Municipality-3, Solukhumbu.

According to Santosh Basyal, information officer at the District Police Office, Mustang, Sharma fell ill on November 4 while returning after visiting the Muktinath Temple in Waragung Muktichhetra Rural Municipality-1.

Similarly, Kulung, who had arrived in Mustang from Manang after crossing the Thorong La Pass on the Annapurna Circuit trek, was found unconscious in a hotel. He had gone to take a shower in the bathroom but did not come out for a long time. He was later rescued in an unconscious state and taken to the Provincial Hospital in Jomsom, where doctors declared him dead.

Although the post-mortem reports of both victims are yet to be received, the symptoms observed in both cases indicated altitude sickness, according to the hospital. With the number of domestic tourists visiting Mustang increasing during the Dashain and Tihar festivals, all five rural municipalities in the district have also reported a growing number of people seeking medical attention for altitude-related problems at local health facilities.

Chief District Officer Parsuram Pokhrel said the authorities had intensified awareness campaigns in response to the situation. Tourists suffering from mild symptoms are provided with primary treatment, while those with serious complications are referred to the Provincial Hospital in Jomsom.

"Altitude sickness is the main challenge for tourists visiting Mustang. Tourists can save their lives by taking necessary precautions," he said.

Elderly people, those with chronic illnesses and people suffering from seasonal ailments are more vulnerable to altitude sickness when travelling in adverse climatic conditions, he added.

Initial symptoms of altitude sickness include mild headaches, fatigue and dizziness. Difficulty walking or breathing, nausea and diarrhoea are also warning signs that require immediate attention.

People experiencing such symptoms should avoid ascending to higher elevations, take adequate rest and drink plenty of water and other fluids. If they feel uncomfortable, they should immediately descend to a lower altitude and seek medical attention.

According to Ajay Thapa, a health assistant at the High Altitude Treatment Centre located at Muktinath Temple, health workers regularly visit the temple premises to provide treatment to pilgrims experiencing altitude-related problems.

He said altitude sickness could be treated if timely precautions and appropriate medical care were taken. However, ignoring the symptoms, remaining at high altitudes or attempting to climb further could lead to life-threatening swelling of the brain or lungs.

The District Administration Office has been conducting awareness and screening campaigns from the Mustang border to Upper Mustang in coordination with local governments, the District Police Office, the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) and health institutions.

Tourists are also provided with information leaflets about local weather conditions, altitude-related risks and necessary precautions.

In the municipality of Gaur in Nepal, 28-year-old Rakesh Yadav sustained severe injuries in a shooting carried out by an unidentified group on the evening of November 3. The attack occurred at around 9:15 p.m. near a water tank in the Gadhawa Tol area, in Ward No. 4 of Gaur Municipality, the Kathmandu Post reports.

Six gunshot wounds

According to Rautahat district police, Yadav suffered six gunshot wounds: three to the back, one to the upper right arm, and two to the legs. Law enforcement officers found three empty pistol shell casings at the scene of the attack.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Victim taken to hospital

The injured man was initially taken to the Provincial Hospital in Gaur. He was later transferred to Nepal Mediciti Vayodha Hospital in Birgunj for further treatment. According to police, Yadav is in critical condition.

The identities of the attackers and the motive for the shooting have not yet been established. Police are investigating the incident.

title: Nepal welcomes 132,000 foreign tourists in October - The Rising Nepal

full_article:
By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Nov. 4: Nepal welcomed over 132,000 international visitors in October 2026, recording a 3.4 per cent increase compared to the same month last year.

According to the Nepal Tourism Board (NTB), a total of 132,814 international tourists visited Nepal in October, marking the highest monthly tourist arrivals in 2026.

The country received 128,443 international visitors in October 2025. The number increased by 4,371 in October this year.

With October arrivals, the total number of international visitors to Nepal crossed 1 million in the first ten months of 2026.

Of these, 92,573 tourists visited in January, while 105,441 visited in February and 120,516 international visitors entered Nepal in March 2026.

Tourist arrivals then reached 107,934 in April, before declining slightly to 102,626 in May and 91,363 in June, 71,775 in July, 85,444 in August 2026 and 88,248 in September.

The October figure was the highest monthly arrival recorded during the first ten months of 2026.

According to the NTB's October 2026 International Visitor Arrivals (IVAs) data, the United States remained the largest source market, with 17,437 visitors, accounting for 13.13 per cent of total arrivals.

India ranked second with 12,097 visitors (9.11 per cent), followed by China with 11,695 (8.81 per cent), the United Kingdom with 9,385 (7.07 per cent) and Australia with 9,352 (7.04 per cent).

In terms of regional distribution, Europe accounted for the largest share of arrivals at 30 per cent (39,877 tourists), followed by other Asian countries at 20.4 per cent (27,040 tourists) and South Asia (SAARC) at 18.11 per cent (24,053 tourists).

The Americas contributed 16 per cent (21,270 tourists) of total arrivals, while Oceania accounted for 7.64 per cent (10143 visitors).

Other regions, the Middle East and Africa contributed 5.78 per cent, 1.76 per cent and 0.32 per cent, respectively.
